# Association for Cognitive and Behavioral Psychotherapy

since 1999
WELCOME
St Petersburg is looking forward to host the IACBT-C 2024 as we believe it will significantly
contribute to the development of cognitive behavioral therapy in our region, as well as throughout
the Russian Federation and in the post-Soviet area.

IACBT-C is an outstanding event in the world of professionals in the field of mental health and
socionomics, a great source for improving skills and gaining new modern knowledge for cognitive
behavioral therapy and psychotherapy in general, a powerful impetus to professional growth and
personal fulfillment.

Respectfully yours,
**Dmitrii Kovpak**
**President of the Association**
**For Cognitive Behavioral Psychotherapy of Russia**
**Dear colleagues! We are proud to inform you about EABCT Congress 2024!**

This years EABCT Congress is taking place in the vibrant city of Belgrade, Serbia, from September
4-7, with the theme, "New Age of CBT - Challenges and Perspectives."
This is an opportunity to:
• Engage with world-renowned speakers and CBT practitioners (registration is open!)
• Share your research and insights (call for abstracts is open!)
• Network with peers
• Experience the rich culture and hospitality of Belgrade.

Your participation will not only contribute to the advancement of CBT but also offer you an
unforgettable experience in one of Europe's most captivating and vibrant cities.

Registration is available on [eabct2024.org][1]

See you in Belgrade!

**Will you help our scientists** to develop a new approach to reducing the stress and fatigue of
being in online meetings all day?


The Idea

Our games are based on the science of Cognitive Behavior Modification, through which new habits of
thought can be learned toward boosting wellbeing. The principles implemented in our games have been
shown to reduce stress, boost confidence and improve performance.

**------------

How you can help

Let your responses contribute to developing more effective games. We are developing adaptive
algorithms to tailor the games to each user's particular characteristics. We do not collect data
about you other than the responses you give. If you have any comments about our games, please send
them along using the form below.

### THE SCIENCE

Our research has contributed to a new approach to assisting people in training a positive identity
and emotional attitude. The starting point is the observation that most social experiences have an
element of ambiguity, which allows for selectivity and bias: When interacting with other people, for
example, one's emotions can be strongly influenced by the particular elements of the interaction
that the brain anticipates, focuses on, interprets, and stores for recall later. It has been known
for decades that people who have a somewhat positive orientation when thinking about their
experiences tend to have higher general wellbeing, and fewer problems with low self-esteem or
anxiety, than people with a negative bias. Building on this background, our research over the past
decade has shown that it is possible for people to train their brain to have a positive rather than
negative social orientation, and that this training can improve wellbeing - sometimes dramatically.
In the scientific psychology literature, the past ten years has seen an exponential growth in
research into the possibility of training cognitive responses to emotional stimuli (this research is
often referred to as Cognitive Bias Modification). +/- Read More?

Our "games" are designed to help you practice specific mental skills. For example, some games
involve practicing disengaging from unhelpful or distracting thoughts of social criticism and
rejection, rather than dwelling on them and worrying about them. Research has shown that practicing
this mental habit can help people to feel less distracted by social threats, and to feel less
stressed. In one set of published studies by social psychologist Mark Baldwin and his collaborators
at McGill University, participants played a prototype version of this tool for 5 minutes either in
the lab or during breaks from work each day for five minutes, to assess the impact on their feelings
of stress during the day. University students preparing for an exam, who used the tool while taking
occasional breaks from studying, felt less stressed about their exam and ended up feeling less
anxious while writing the exam compared to others who used a placebo task. Telemarketing operators
who used the tool before their work shift reported feeling less stressed and more self-confident
over the course of a week. Remarkably, they also had lowered levels of the stress hormone cortisol
and they even made more sales at work. This research suggests, then, that having a habit of mind
that allows us to avoid being overly distracted by unhelpful thoughts of social rejection can help
us deal with the stresses of daily life, and stay focused on other things we would prefer to pay
attention to.

Other games are more focused on the "activation" of experiences of social connection or acceptance,
since bringing such experiences into working memory can help us to avoid any tendency to anticipate
and focus on negative expectations of rejection or criticism. Still other games involve pairing
images of acceptance with thoughts about oneself: This way thoughts about oneself can come to
trigger associated images of social connection.

Note that of course there is no guarantee that the tool will have these kinds of effects on any

of stress during the day. University students preparing for an exam, who used the tool while taking
occasional breaks from studying, felt less stressed about their exam and ended up feeling less
anxious while writing the exam compared to others who used a placebo task. Telemarketing operators
who used the tool before their work shift reported feeling less stressed and more self-confident
over the course of a week. Remarkably, they also had lowered levels of the stress hormone cortisol
and they even made more sales at work. This research suggests, then, that having a habit of mind
that allows us to avoid being overly distracted by unhelpful thoughts of social rejection can help
us deal with the stresses of daily life, and stay focused on other things we would prefer to pay
attention to.

Other games are more focused on the "activation" of experiences of social connection or acceptance,
since bringing such experiences into working memory can help us to avoid any tendency to anticipate
and focus on negative expectations of rejection or criticism. Still other games involve pairing
images of acceptance with thoughts about oneself: This way thoughts about oneself can come to
trigger associated images of social connection.

Note that of course there is no guarantee that the tool will have these kinds of effects on any
specific individual: This is why our goal is to develop an algorithm to tailor the games to each
individual's characteristics and pattern of responses. Over time we will ask users of this website
to help us by agreeing to contribute their anonymous responses, which will allow us to develop the
algorithm.

### Welcome to ACBM

# Association for Cognitive Bias Modification

ACBM and its members strive to refining assessments of cognitive biases associated with
dysfunctional psychological processes, optimise training procedures to modify cognitive biases, and
leverage the understanding of mechanisms to maximise their therapeutic benefits.

[Learn more about ACBM...][20]

## Why to become a member
* Annual Meeting
* Workshops
* Online resources
* News
* And more...

We bring together clinicians and researchers from around the world who are interested in the
experimental measurement of cognitive biases, the development and testing of cognitive bias
modification protocols, and their clinical and real world application.

[ Join now ][21]

## MEETINGS AND EVENTS

Various events take place around the world that provide opportunities for professionals to learn the
latest in CBM research, hear about clinical insights and innovations, and network with colleagues.

### Welcome to ACBM

# Association for Cognitive Bias Modification

ACBM and its members strive to refining assessments of cognitive biases associated with
dysfunctional psychological processes, optimise training procedures to modify cognitive biases, and
leverage the understanding of mechanisms to maximise their therapeutic benefits.

[Learn more about ACBM...][20]

## Why to become a member
* Annual Meeting
* Workshops
* Online resources
* News
* And more...

We bring together clinicians and researchers from around the world who are interested in the
experimental measurement of cognitive biases, the development and testing of cognitive bias
modification protocols, and their clinical and real world application.

[ Join now ][21]

## MEETINGS AND EVENTS

Various events take place around the world that provide opportunities for professionals to learn the
latest in CBM research, hear about clinical insights and innovations, and network with colleagues.

# Association for Cognitive and Behavioral Psychotherapy

since 1999
WELCOME
St Petersburg is looking forward to host the IACBT-C 2024 as we believe it will significantly
contribute to the development of cognitive behavioral therapy in our region, as well as throughout
the Russian Federation and in the post-Soviet area.

IACBT-C is an outstanding event in the world of professionals in the field of mental health and
socionomics, a great source for improving skills and gaining new modern knowledge for cognitive
behavioral therapy and psychotherapy in general, a powerful impetus to professional growth and
personal fulfillment.

Respectfully yours,
**Dmitrii Kovpak**
**President of the Association**
**For Cognitive Behavioral Psychotherapy of Russia**
**Dear colleagues! We are proud to inform you about EABCT Congress 2024!**

This years EABCT Congress is taking place in the vibrant city of Belgrade, Serbia, from September
4-7, with the theme, "New Age of CBT - Challenges and Perspectives."
This is an opportunity to:
• Engage with world-renowned speakers and CBT practitioners (registration is open!)
• Share your research and insights (call for abstracts is open!)
• Network with peers
• Experience the rich culture and hospitality of Belgrade.

Your participation will not only contribute to the advancement of CBT but also offer you an
unforgettable experience in one of Europe's most captivating and vibrant cities.

Registration is available on [eabct2024.org][1]

See you in Belgrade!

## Breeze App Supports Mental Well-being
## To Thrive

### Mood Tracking

A breeze tool to keep track of your emotions and moods throughout the day. Build a habit of tracking
your feelings daily with our easy-to-use tool to uncover all the patterns and triggers driving your
emotional state.

Now, it is so easy to be aware of all your ups and downs while discovering the power of
understanding yourself on a whole new level.

[Mood Tracking]

### Quick Self-Checkups

Snappy personal checkups to keep you in the know. If you're confused about what you're feeling or
which symptoms you might have, you can check in with us.

We'll help you figure things out and give suggestions on what to do next. It's time to embark on a
process of self-awareness with quick informative tests to check your mental well-being.

[Quick Self-Checkups]

### Self-Growth Courses

Expert courses on various mental well-being topics 101: from Love & Relationships to Anxiety and
Depression. Based on CBT principles, each course lasts just 8–10 minutes for easier comprehension.

Discover empowering self-growth educational resources focused on fostering and nurturing your
psychological well-being.

[Self-Growth Courses]

### Mental Well-being Tests

Comprehensive and accurate science-based tests on mental well-being topics. We collect and adopt the
best personality (and not only) test for in-depth self-understanding. You can use these
questionnaires to look for trends or patterns in your behavior. In turn, you receive helpful
insights to nurture your mental well-being from us.

It's easier than ever before to explore the realms of your personality and beyond with
self-assessment tools.

[Mental Well-being Tests]

### Relaxation Games

Breeze App collection of games designed to help you unwind from anxiety and alleviate stress. If you
are anxious or stressed, you can use relaxation breathing techniques to calm yourself down.

These engaging games are a captivating way to reach your inner calm through a variety of mindfulness
exercises.

[Relaxation Games]

### Insights in Numbers

Maximize the potential of data with our visually compelling statistics. They not only depict your
emotional trends but also underline key influencers of your well-being. Ready to harness the power
of insights from numbers? Let the numbers guide you to a more balanced and fulfilling life.

[Insights in Numbers]

### What is CheckerTR PRO?

CheckerTR PRO is an all-in-one GSM repair toolkit for professional technicians. It covers IMEI
repair, FRP bypass, data recovery, and flashing for most Android brands.

### Which brands are supported?

We support Samsung, Xiaomi, MediaTek, Qualcomm, Huawei, Oppo, Realme, Infinix, Tecno, and many other
brands with dedicated service modules.

### How can I get a license?

Licenses and credits are sold through our official reseller network. Check our [Authorized

examples include [confirmation bias][14], [anchoring bias][15], and [availability heuristic][16]. By
understanding these biases, you can make more rational choices, avoid common mental traps, and
ultimately improve your decision-making process.

## Common Questions About Cognitive Biases

### What are cognitive biases and why do they matter?

Cognitive biases are mental shortcuts or patterns in our thinking that can lead to errors in
judgment and decision-making. They matter because they impact nearly every aspect of our lives—from
personal choices to business decisions, social interactions, and even health outcomes. Common
examples include [confirmation bias][14], [anchoring bias][15], and [availability heuristic][16]. By
understanding these biases, you can make more rational choices, avoid common mental traps, and
ultimately improve your decision-making process.

### How can I use this site to improve my decision-making?

Great question! Our site offers several practical ways to boost your decision-making skills:
* Learn about specific biases: Browse our [comprehensive library][17] to understand how each bias
  affects your thinking.
* Try interactive exercises: Experience biases firsthand through our [quiz][18] and various
  simulations.
* Practice prevention strategies: Each bias page includes practical tips for overcoming that
  particular mental trap.
* Regular practice: Return regularly to reinforce your learning—understanding cognitive biases is an
  ongoing process!

[Take the Quiz][19][Play Matching Game][20][Try a Bias Test][21]

### Are some people more susceptible to cognitive biases than others?

Everyone experiences cognitive biases—they're part of being human! While no one is immune, research
suggests that factors like stress, time pressure, and cognitive load can make us more vulnerable to
these thinking errors. For instance, [Dunning-Kruger effect][22] shows how experts and novices
assess their abilities differently. The good news? Awareness is the first step toward improvement.
By learning to recognize these biases, anyone can work to mitigate their effects, regardless of
their natural tendencies. Education, critical thinking skills, and mindfulness practices have all
been shown to help reduce the impact of cognitive biases.

### How long does it take to overcome cognitive biases?

Overcoming cognitive biases isn't a one-time achievement but rather an ongoing process. While you
can start recognizing your own biases within days of learning about them, developing consistent
habits to counter these biases might take months or even become a lifelong practice. Biases like
[status quo bias][23] and [sunk cost fallacy][24] are particularly persistent because they're deeply
rooted in our psychology. Remember, the goal isn't to eliminate biases completely (that's
practically impossible!) but to recognize when they're influencing you and apply techniques to
minimize their impact. Even professional psychologists and behavioral economists continue to work on
their own biases—it's part of the human journey! We recommend regularly taking our [cognitive bias
quiz][25] to gauge your progress.

### Can cognitive biases ever be helpful?

Yes! Cognitive biases evolved for a reason. In many cases, these mental shortcuts help us make quick
decisions when time or information is limited. For example, the [availability heuristic][26] helps

# Homepage

DABATEM *(**Istanbul Center for Behavioral Sciences*** – formerly the *Istanbul Center for Behavior
Research and Therapy*) is an independent research center internationally recognized for its
pioneering research into mental health effects of wars, torture, and earthquakes, and their
effective treatment. It has been founded and is currently directed by [Professor Metin Başoğlu][56].

Mass trauma events affect large numbers of people and lead to a serious mental health problem around
the world. Effective dealing with this problem requires a mental healthcare model based on
interventions that are (1) theoretically sound, (2) proven to be effective, (3) brief, (4) easy to
train therapists in their delivery, (5) practicable in different cultures, and (6) suitable for
dissemination through media other than professional therapists, such as lay people, self-help tools,
and mass media. Current trauma treatments do not meet more than two or three of these requirements.

DABATEM has conducted extensive research over 40 years with trauma survivors to develop a
psychological treatment ([Control-Focused Behavioral Treatment – CFBT][57]), which meets all of the
above requirements. CFBT is a brief intervention that reduces traumatic stress by enhancing** sense
of control** over (or resilience against) trauma.  [Available evidence][58] suggests that it
achieves greater improvement than other evidence-based treatments.

DABATEM has also developed a [mental healthcare model][59] for earthquake survivors that
incorporates various brief and innovative applications of CFBT and treatment delivery strategies
that enable cost-effective dissemination of care to large survivor populations. Work is in progress
to develop a similar model for survivors of war and torture. A recent [treatment study][60] has
shown that CFBT is highly effective in survivors of war and torture.

social and political scientists, human rights workers, international law experts, policy makers, and
governmental and nongovernmental organizations concerned with care of mass trauma survivors. An

to develop a similar model for survivors of war and torture. A recent [treatment study][60] has
shown that CFBT is highly effective in survivors of war and torture.

Mass trauma events raise important issues of concern to mental and public health professionals,
social and political scientists, human rights workers, international law experts, policy makers, and
governmental and nongovernmental organizations concerned with care of mass trauma survivors. An
important aspect of DABATEM’s mission is to inform the world public, [media][61], and professional
opinion on these issues. Professor Başoğlu’s articles on some of these issues can be found
[here][62] or in his [personal website.][63] Some of his scientific publications can be downloaded
from [ResearchGate][64].

# [More Thoughts on Suicide Prediction and Suicide Screening (from Craig Bryan, Ph.D.)][27]

[July 1, 2026][28] [johnsommersflanagan][29] [6 Comments][30]

Hi All,

Below, I’ve a pasted LinkedIn post from Dr. Craig Bryan, author of “Rethinking Suicide” and a
leading suicide researcher. At the bottom of his comments there’s a link to the article of which he
speaks.

Enjoy!

*****************

From Craig Bryan, LinkedIn – 6/29/2026

We keep trying to predict who will attempt suicide. A 15-year study suggests we’re asking the wrong
question.

Researchers followed 2,060 Brazilian children from age 10 into their mid-twenties—one of the longest
prospective suicide studies ever conducted outside a high-income country. They measured genetics,
perinatal history, family psychiatric illness, childhood adversity, cognition, and clinical
symptoms, then tested all of it together against who later attempted suicide.

The result: even with multiple domains of risk factors combined, prediction accuracy stayed modest
(AUC 0.665), barely above the ceiling seen across 50 years of suicide research. More sophisticated
machine learning models didn’t do any better than simple logistic regression.

Three factors stood out as consistent, actionable, and population-relevant: childhood threat
exposure (especially bullying), caregiver history of suicide attempts, and childhood externalizing
disorders. Bullying alone accounted for the largest share of preventable risk in the entire study.

The authors’ conclusion is blunt: distal childhood risk factors will likely never predict individual
suicide attempts with precision, because suicide is driven by acute, fast-moving processes that a
baseline assessment can’t capture. Trying to screen our way to safety has a ceiling. We hit it
decades ago.

The better investment may not be sharper prediction. It may be quieter, structural prevention like
anti-bullying programs, supporting parents with histories of suicidal behavior, and early
identification of behavioral disorders, the kind of intervention that helps a population, whether or
not we ever know which child needed it most.

**************************

Here’s the article link: [**https://lnkd.in/eRWtBiXK**][31]

I’m excited about Dr. Bryan’s post not because of the difficulties with prediction (which we’ve long
know), but because of the idea of moving upstream toward structural prevention. I also feel this
fits really well with what we’re trying to do with CAPE.

**Obviously, I love this quotation: **“Trying to screen our way to safety has a ceiling. We hit it
decades ago.”

Have a great evening!

JSF

club mentality that interfered with women’s salaries and promotions.

Let’s all agree on the following: All discrimination is wrong, allegations should be taken
seriously, and allegations deserve investigation.

But allegations are not facts.

Sadly, numerous Facebook posts, including an Op-Ed piece published in a Montana newspaper, repeat
allegations from 2021 to 2024 (when the case was settled). Beyond these allegations, they don’t

you to believe, that Seth Bodnar is, among other unpleasant characterizations, sexist and
misogynistic.

# Drink Less,
# Live More

#### Reframe the way you think and drink through neuroscience

## We do science, not stigma.

#### Developed with hundreds of medical and mental health experts, Reframe is a revolutionary
#### alcohol-related habit change app.

### All-In-One

The only platform that utilizes neuroscience, bringing together an evidence-based behavior change
program, tools, and a supportive community.

### Evidence-Based Alcohol Reduction Program

Our world-renowned program is developed by leading experts in the fields of psychology and
neuroscience.

### Reframe Works. Period.

The proof is in the data! Even when compared to other apps, Reframe users reported a significantly
lower amount of alcohol consumption.
With Reframe’s neuroscience-based program, habit changes stick.
‍

So far, Reframe has already helped millions around the world make lasting changes to their drinking
habits.

## **91% of Reframe users noted a substantial decrease in alcohol use within 3 months.**

### Neuroscience-Based Alcohol Reduction Program

The heart of Reframe is our exclusive program, developed by leading experts in the fields of mental
health and medicine. Visit your Daily Tasks to learn something new every day.

### Personalized Drink Tracker

Stay accountable day-by-day and keep track of your progress over time.

### In-Depth Courses Covering Every Area

Learn something new with Reframe Courses — recorded and live videos about everything you need to
build a meaningful life while drinking less.

### 24/7 Private Community

Level up your alcohol-free or mindful drinking life with friends! Celebrate milestones or give and
receive support. The journey is always better together!

### Comprehensive Toolkit for All Your Needs

Everything you need to beat cravings is at the touch of a button! Tune into a meditation, keep your
hands busy with a game, or watch an inspiring video.

# Laws of UX

Laws of UX is a collection of best practices that designers can consider when building user
interfaces.

The updated Laws of UX large format index poster is now available! Additions include Paradox of the
Active User, Selective Attention, Cognitive Bias, and more. [Check it out →][19]
* ## [Aesthetic-Usability Effect][20]
  
  Users often perceive aesthetically pleasing design as design that’s more usable.
* ## [Choice Overload][21]
  
  The tendency for people to get overwhelmed when they are presented with a large number of options,
  often used interchangeably with the term paradox of choice.
* ## [Chunking][22]
  
  A process by which individual pieces of an information set are broken down and then grouped
  together in a meaningful whole.
* ## [Cognitive Bias][23]
  
  A systematic error of thinking or rationality in judgment that influence our perception of the
  world and our decision-making ability.
* ## [Cognitive Load][24]
  
  The amount of mental resources needed to understand and interact with an interface.
* ## [Doherty Threshold][25]
  
  Productivity soars when a computer and its users interact at a pace (<400ms) that ensures that
  neither has to wait on the other.
* ## [Fitts’s Law][26]
  
  The time to acquire a target is a function of the distance to and size of the target.
* ## [Flow][27]
  
  The mental state in which a person performing some activity is fully immersed in a feeling of
  energized focus, full involvement, and enjoyment in the process of the activity.
* ## [Goal-Gradient Effect][28]
  
  The tendency to approach a goal increases with proximity to the goal.
* ## [Hick’s Law][29]
  
  The time it takes to make a decision increases with the number and complexity of choices.
* ## [Jakob’s Law][30]
  
  Users spend most of their time on other sites. This means that users prefer your site to work the
  same way as all the other sites they already know.
* ## [Law of Common Region][31]
  
  Elements tend to be perceived into groups if they are sharing an area with a clearly defined
  boundary.
* ## [Law of Proximity][32]
  
  Objects that are near, or proximate to each other, tend to be grouped together.
* ## [Law of Prägnanz][33]
  
  People will perceive and interpret ambiguous or complex images as the simplest form possible,
  because it is the interpretation that requires the least cognitive effort of us.
* ## [Law of Similarity][34]
  
  The human eye tends to perceive similar elements as a complete picture, shape, or group, even if
  those elements are separated.
* ## [Law of Uniform Connectedness][35]
  
  Elements that are visually connected are perceived as more related than elements with no
  connection.
* ## [Mental Model][36]
  
  A compressed model based on what we think we know about a system and how it works.
* ## [Miller’s Law][37]
  
  The average person can only keep 7 (plus or minus 2) items in their working memory.
* ## [Occam’s Razor][38]
  
  Among competing hypotheses that predict equally well, the one with the fewest assumptions should
  be selected.
* ## [Paradox of the Active User][39]
  
  Users never read manuals but start using the software immediately.
* ## [Pareto Principle][40]
  
  The Pareto principle states that, for many events, roughly 80% of the effects come from 20% of the
  causes.
* ## [Parkinson’s Law][41]
  
  Any task will inflate until all of the available time is spent.
* ## [Peak-End Rule][42]
  
  People judge an experience largely based on how they felt at its peak and at its end, rather than
  the total sum or average of every moment of the experience.
* ## [Postel’s Law][43]
  
  Be liberal in what you accept, and conservative in what you send.
* ## [Selective Attention][44]
  
  The process of focusing our attention only to a subset of stimuli in an environment — usually
  those related to our goals.
* ## [Serial Position Effect][45]
  
  Users have a propensity to best remember the first and last items in a series.
* ## [Tesler’s Law][46]
  
  Tesler's Law, also known as The Law of Conservation of Complexity, states that for any system
  there is a certain amount of complexity which cannot be reduced.
* ## [Von Restorff Effect][47]
  
  The Von Restorff effect, also known as The Isolation Effect, predicts that when multiple similar
  objects are present, the one that differs from the rest is most likely to be remembered.
* ## [Working Memory][48]
  
  A cognitive system that temporarily holds and manipulates information needed to complete tasks.
* ## [Zeigarnik Effect][49]
  
  People remember uncompleted or interrupted tasks better than completed tasks.

# Laws of UX

Laws of UX is a collection of best practices that designers can consider when building user
interfaces.

The updated Laws of UX large format index poster is now available! Additions include Paradox of the
Active User, Selective Attention, Cognitive Bias, and more. [Check it out →][19]
* ## [Aesthetic-Usability Effect][20]
  
  Users often perceive aesthetically pleasing design as design that’s more usable.
* ## [Choice Overload][21]
  
  The tendency for people to get overwhelmed when they are presented with a large number of options,
  often used interchangeably with the term paradox of choice.
* ## [Chunking][22]
  
  A process by which individual pieces of an information set are broken down and then grouped
  together in a meaningful whole.
* ## [Cognitive Bias][23]
  
  A systematic error of thinking or rationality in judgment that influence our perception of the
  world and our decision-making ability.
* ## [Cognitive Load][24]
  
  The amount of mental resources needed to understand and interact with an interface.
* ## [Doherty Threshold][25]
  
  Productivity soars when a computer and its users interact at a pace (<400ms) that ensures that
  neither has to wait on the other.
* ## [Fitts’s Law][26]
  
  The time to acquire a target is a function of the distance to and size of the target.
* ## [Flow][27]
  
  The mental state in which a person performing some activity is fully immersed in a feeling of
  energized focus, full involvement, and enjoyment in the process of the activity.
* ## [Goal-Gradient Effect][28]
  
  The tendency to approach a goal increases with proximity to the goal.
* ## [Hick’s Law][29]
  
  The time it takes to make a decision increases with the number and complexity of choices.
* ## [Jakob’s Law][30]
  
  Users spend most of their time on other sites. This means that users prefer your site to work the
  same way as all the other sites they already know.
* ## [Law of Common Region][31]
  
  Elements tend to be perceived into groups if they are sharing an area with a clearly defined
  boundary.
* ## [Law of Proximity][32]
  
  Objects that are near, or proximate to each other, tend to be grouped together.
* ## [Law of Prägnanz][33]
  
  People will perceive and interpret ambiguous or complex images as the simplest form possible,
  because it is the interpretation that requires the least cognitive effort of us.
* ## [Law of Similarity][34]
  
  The human eye tends to perceive similar elements as a complete picture, shape, or group, even if
  those elements are separated.
* ## [Law of Uniform Connectedness][35]
  
  Elements that are visually connected are perceived as more related than elements with no
  connection.
* ## [Mental Model][36]

## 
## Richard J. McNally
## *Professor and Director of Clinical Training *

Dr. McNally studies anxiety disorders (e.g., social anxiety disorder), obsessive-compulsive disorder
(OCD), posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD), complicated grief, and depression. A major emphasis is
elucidating cognitive biases constitutive of these syndromes, and testing methods for reducing these
biases, thereby fostering symptom reduction. Hence, much of our work falls under the rubric of
experimental psychopathology as it aims to illuminate the mechanisms driving the etiology and
maintenance of emotional disorders. By clicking on the Research link above, you can read about
recent and ongoing projects in our lab.

Our research has contributed to a new approach to assisting people in training a positive identity

element of ambiguity, which allows for selectivity and bias: When interacting with other people, for
example, one's emotions can be strongly influenced by the particular elements of the interaction
that the brain anticipates, focuses on, interprets, and stores for recall later. It has been known
for decades that people who have a somewhat positive orientation when thinking about their
experiences tend to have higher general wellbeing, and fewer problems with low self-esteem or
anxiety, than people with a negative bias. Building on this background, our research over the past
decade has shown that it is possible for people to train their brain to have a positive rather than
negative social orientation, and that this training can improve wellbeing - sometimes dramatically.
In the scientific psychology literature, the past ten years has seen an exponential growth in
research into the possibility of training cognitive responses to emotional stimuli (this research is
often referred to as Cognitive Bias Modification). +/- Read More?

Our "games" are designed to help you practice specific mental skills. For example, some games
involve practicing disengaging from unhelpful or distracting thoughts of social criticism and
rejection, rather than dwelling on them and worrying about them. Research has shown that practicing
this mental habit can help people to feel less distracted by social threats, and to feel less
stressed. In one set of published studies by social psychologist Mark Baldwin and his collaborators
at McGill University, participants played a prototype version of this tool for 5 minutes either in

of stress during the day. University students preparing for an exam, who used the tool while taking

anxious while writing the exam compared to others who used a placebo task. Telemarketing operators
who used the tool before their work shift reported feeling less stressed and more self-confident
over the course of a week. Remarkably, they also had lowered levels of the stress hormone cortisol
and they even made more sales at work. This research suggests, then, that having a habit of mind
that allows us to avoid being overly distracted by unhelpful thoughts of social rejection can help
us deal with the stresses of daily life, and stay focused on other things we would prefer to pay
attention to.

since bringing such experiences into working memory can help us to avoid any tendency to anticipate
and focus on negative expectations of rejection or criticism. Still other games involve pairing

trigger associated images of social connection.

RESILIENCE & HOPE

# Courage to heal. Strength to continue.

Misneach Mental Health is a therapy practice grounded in the belief that healing begins with
courage—the courage to show up, to face what hurts, and to keep moving forward even when the path
feels uncertain. The word Misneach (pronounced MISH-nukh) comes from Irish Gaelic and represents
courage, bravery, spirit, fortitude, hopefulness, and confidence. It reflects the inner strength
that allows people to rise again after being knocked down and to meet life’s challenges with
resilience and integrity. At Misneach Mental Health, the practice honors the bravery it takes to
seek support and the quiet strength found in choosing growth, healing, and self-understanding.

[Begin Your Healing
][3]
The Approach

## The Meaning of Misneach

Misneach (mish-nyokh) is a Gaelic word representing courage, spirit, and mental fortitude. It is
more than just bravery; it is the inner strength required to face adversity with hope and the
resilience to continue even when the path is difficult. At Misneach Mental Health, our philosophy is
rooted in this concept—honoring each individual's innate capacity for healing and growth. We believe
that therapy is a collaborative journey where professional expertise meets the client's personal
courage, creating a space where transformation and lasting well-being become possible.

## About Kim

Kim is trained in Adaptive Internal Relational Network Therapy (AIR) and Eye Movement
Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR). She has worked extensively with children, adolescents, and
families in school settings, and has also served the State of Minnesota through roles with both the
Department of Corrections and the Department of Health Services. Kim’s clinical work is grounded in
a strengths-based perspective, incorporating motivational interviewing and solution-focused
interventions, with a strong foundation in Adlerian therapy. She is deeply committed to helping
clients develop their capacity to heal from trauma and move toward becoming their most authentic,
empowered selves. Kim holds a Master’s degree in Adlerian Psychology with a focus on Co-Occurring
Disorders from Adler Graduate School, a Master’s degree in Forensic Psychology from Argosy
University, and a Bachelor of Arts in Criminal Justice from St. Cloud State University. She received
her EMDR training through an EMDRIA-approved provider. Kim is honored to support the men and women
who serve their communities and country, including military personnel, veterans, first responders,
firefighters, and law enforcement officers. She recognizes the distinct challenges inherent in these
professions and is committed to providing a safe, respectful, and confidential space for healing and
restoration. Misneach Mental Health is dedicated to evidence-based, trauma-informed care tailored to
the needs of active-duty service members, veterans, and public safety professionals. The practice
understands the occupational stress, cumulative trauma, and high-risk demands that can impact mental
health. Clients can expect a supportive, confidential environment focused on resilience, effective
coping, and long-term psychological well-being.

##### Cognitive-Behavioral Therapies

Focus on identifying and changing unhelpful thought patterns and behaviors.

##### Cognitive Restructuring

##### Behavioral Activation

##### Mindfulness

Focusing on the present moment.

##### Psychodynamic Therapy

Explores past experiences and relationships to understand current patterns.

##### Humanistic Therapy

Emphasizes self-exploration, personal growth, and unconditional positive regard.

##### Interpersonal Therapy (IPT)

Focuses on improving relationships and social functioning, often for depression.

##### Communication & Skills Training

Focuses on building interpersonal skills, conflict resolution, and problem-solving for individuals
or families.

##### EMDR (Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing)

Helps reprocess traumatic memories.

##### Psychoeducation

Teaching clients about their conditions and coping skills.

##### Motivational Interviewing (MI)

Helps clients find internal motivation for change.

##### Supportive Therapy

Provides empathy, validation, and active listening.

##### Adlerian

Goal-oriented, strengths-based intervention that helps individuals understand lifestyle, sense of

##### DBT skills

A structured, evidence-based intervention that teaches mindfulness, distress tolerance, emotion
regulation, and interpersonal effectiveness to help individuals manage intense emotions.

##### Behavioral Activation

##### Mindfulness

Focusing on the present moment.

## Voices of Hope

"The courage to heal and the strength to thrive are real. This journey has been one of profound
resilience and the quiet strength of a supportive community."

Sarah J.

"The telehealth model made it accessible and convenient. The clinic provided a professional
environment that felt like home, where breathing became easier again."

Elena R.

"Misneach Mental Health provided the compassionate space needed to rebuild a foundation. It is a
practice that truly honors the human spirit."

David M.

"Hope is a tangible thing. Through specialized work with the clinic, one can learn to navigate
life's challenges with a renewed sense of courage and strength."

James K.

## Delivery Formats

• Individual Therapy: One-on-one sessions.

## Goals
* • Improve Coping: Develop healthier ways to handle stress, trauma, and difficult emotional
  activation cues.
* 
* • Enhance Self-Awareness: Increase understanding of oneself, patterns, and activation cues.
* 
* • Modify Behavior: Reduce self-destructive actions and build positive habits.
* 
* • Strengthen Relationships: Improve communication and connection in family or couple counseling.
* 
* • Support Holistic Well-being: Address emotional and social health alongside physical recovery.

# Feel better with interactive mental health tools

Simple practices you can use right now. Calm the body, steady emotions, and focus on small steps.
Tools are evidence based, private by design, and fast on phones.

[Open Toolkit][16] [Get Support][17]

**Important:** if you are in immediate danger, contact local emergency services.

[TIPP][18] [5 4 3 2 1][19] [Breathing][20] [Safe Place][21] [Relax][22] [Urge][23] [Facts][24]
[Opposite][25]

## Choose a simple path

[
🧭

### Self Discovery Tests

Quick check ins to learn about mood, stress, and habits.

][26] [
🎯

### Wellness Games and Exercises

Practice skills for focus, calm, and motivation.

][27] [
🤝

### Get Support

Find a professional for private, personal help.

][28]

## Popular right now
* [
  
  ### Breathing Anchor
  
  Steady breath, settle nerves, and regain focus.
  
  ][29]
* [
  
  ### Focus Timer
  
  Work in short sprints with gentle breaks.
  
  ][30]
* [
  
  ### Thought Reframe Studio
  
  Spot thinking traps and try a kinder view.
  
  ][31]
* [
  
  ### Gratitude Galaxy
  
  Log small wins and watch your stars grow.
  
  ][32]
* [
  
  ### Opposite Action Planner
  
  Choose the next helpful action when urges pull you off track.
  
  ][33]
* [
  
  ### Digital Zen Garden
  
  Play and settle attention with a calm space.
  
  ][34]
* [
  
  ### Sensory Grounding
  
  Use the five senses to return to the present.
  
  ][35]
* [
  
  ### TIPP Crisis Kit
  
  Lower arousal fast with safe, short actions.
  
  ][36]

## How interactive mental health tools help

The site focuses on small skills you can practice in minutes. You can calm the body, label thoughts,
and plan the next step. The tools draw from CBT, DBT, mindfulness, and behavior change. Pages are
private by design and mobile first.

## Frequently asked questions

Do these tools replace therapy

No. These are self help practices. They do not diagnose or replace care. Use Get Support if you want
to work with a professional.

How is my data handled

If a tool saves entries, it uses your browser. Nothing goes to a server. You can clear data by
clearing site storage.

What if I feel worse

Pause and try a calming tool like Breathing Anchor or 5 4 3 2 1 Grounding. If distress continues,
contact local emergency services.

How often should I practice

Short and steady works best. Try 2 to 10 minutes once or twice a day. Repeat what helps.

Where should I start

Pick one tool that fits now. For high arousal try TIPP. For thinking traps try Thought Reframe
Studio.

## Trust and science

Learn more from [NIMH][37], [APA][38], [WHO][39].

## Important safety information

These tools are educational self help. They are not therapy or a diagnosis. If you face an
emergency, contact local emergency services. For non emergency help, visit Get Support.

Exercises][42] · [Get Support][43]

[0a361b1821a63e43dbb2f5904b136ab15]

[Glavnaya21]

Вы пытались справиться самостоятельно, читали умные книги, уговаривали себя успокоиться, но не
смотря на усилия, паника, страх и тревога возвращаются снова. Обратитесь за психологической помощью.

Если вы сталкиваетесь с:

## Паническими атаками

[image(1)]

У вас непредсказуемые приступы сильного страха, сопровождаемые такими симптомами: сердцебиение,
ощущение удушья, тремор, потливость, головокружение, слабость, тошнота, дереализация и
деперсонализация. Приступы сопровождаются страхом смерти, потери контроля или сумасшествия.

## Страхом общения

[0a361b1821a63e43dbb2f5904b136ab15]

Вы боитесь оценки со стороны других людей. Вас пугает, что в процессе общения у вас будут трястись
руки, дрожать голос, вы покраснеете, вспотеете, скажете глупость или будете казаться неловким.
Бывает, что вы откладываете важные звонки, избегаете выступлений или поездок в метро.

## Тревогой и беспокойством

[Glavnaya21]

Вы постоянно в тревоге по самым разным причинам. То вы беспокоитесь о работе, то про здоровье, то о
благополучии близких, то не можете уснуть перед поездкой в отпуск. Вы устали от бесконечного
«мысленного диалога», при котором ваш внутренний голос постоянно рисует катастрофические сценарии.

Вы пытались справиться самостоятельно, читали умные книги, уговаривали себя успокоиться, но не
смотря на усилия, паника, страх и тревога возвращаются снова. Обратитесь за психологической помощью.

[42]: javascript:; yourlogicalfallacyis.com [ [Thou shalt not commit logical fallacies] ][1]

A logical fallacy is a flaw in reasoning. Logical fallacies are like tricks or illusions of thought,
and they're often very sneakily used by politicians and the media to fool people. Don't be fooled!
This website has been designed to help you identify and call out dodgy logic wherever it may raise
its ugly, incoherent head. Rollover the icons above and click for examples. If you see someone
committing a fallacy, link them to it e.g. yourlogicalfallacyis.com/strawman
* ## [ Critical Thinking Workshops ][2]
  
  Critical thinking is becoming critically important because as more work gets automated, your
  people’s judgment is what great risk and opportunity both hinge upon.
  
  ###### [See the options][3]
* ## [ Critical Thinking Cards ][4]
  
  Get a deck of these pretty great high quality cards featuring 24 logical fallacies and 24
  cognitive biases, as well as 3 game cards. Play watching cable news or a political debate!
  
  ###### [Visit the Thinking Shop][5]
* ## [ Thou shalt not suffer cognitive biases ][6]
  
  Biases make our judgments irrational. Check out our sister site featuring 24 of the most common
  biases that affect decision making, beliefs and thinking.
  
  ###### [Visit yourbias.is][7]

## Download all our resources for free

Including printable Critical Thinking Cards, Fallacies & Biases wall posters & more. Published under
Creative Commons by our non profit.

### Welcome to ACBM

# Association for Cognitive Bias Modification

ACBM and its members strive to refining assessments of cognitive biases associated with
dysfunctional psychological processes, optimise training procedures to modify cognitive biases, and
leverage the understanding of mechanisms to maximise their therapeutic benefits.

[Learn more about ACBM...][20]

## Why to become a member
* Annual Meeting
* Workshops
* Online resources
* News
* And more...

We bring together clinicians and researchers from around the world who are interested in the
experimental measurement of cognitive biases, the development and testing of cognitive bias
modification protocols, and their clinical and real world application.

[ Join now ][21]

## MEETINGS AND EVENTS

Various events take place around the world that provide opportunities for professionals to learn the
latest in CBM research, hear about clinical insights and innovations, and network with colleagues.

[Learn more ...][22]

## Breeze App Supports Mental Well-being
## To Thrive

### Mood Tracking

A breeze tool to keep track of your emotions and moods throughout the day. Build a habit of tracking
your feelings daily with our easy-to-use tool to uncover all the patterns and triggers driving your
emotional state.

Now, it is so easy to be aware of all your ups and downs while discovering the power of
understanding yourself on a whole new level.

[Mood Tracking]

### Quick Self-Checkups

Snappy personal checkups to keep you in the know. If you're confused about what you're feeling or
which symptoms you might have, you can check in with us.

We'll help you figure things out and give suggestions on what to do next. It's time to embark on a
process of self-awareness with quick informative tests to check your mental well-being.

[Quick Self-Checkups]

### Self-Growth Courses

Expert courses on various mental well-being topics 101: from Love & Relationships to Anxiety and
Depression. Based on CBT principles, each course lasts just 8–10 minutes for easier comprehension.

Discover empowering self-growth educational resources focused on fostering and nurturing your
psychological well-being.

[Self-Growth Courses]

### Mental Well-being Tests

Comprehensive and accurate science-based tests on mental well-being topics. We collect and adopt the
best personality (and not only) test for in-depth self-understanding. You can use these

## Frequently Asked Questions

## Common Questions About Cognitive Biases

### What are cognitive biases and why do they matter?

Cognitive biases are mental shortcuts or patterns in our thinking that can lead to errors in
judgment and decision-making. They matter because they impact nearly every aspect of our lives—from
personal choices to business decisions, social interactions, and even health outcomes. Common
examples include [confirmation bias][14], [anchoring bias][15], and [availability heuristic][16]. By
understanding these biases, you can make more rational choices, avoid common mental traps, and
ultimately improve your decision-making process.

### How can I use this site to improve my decision-making?

Great question! Our site offers several practical ways to boost your decision-making skills:
* Learn about specific biases: Browse our [comprehensive library][17] to understand how each bias
  affects your thinking.
* Try interactive exercises: Experience biases firsthand through our [quiz][18] and various
  simulations.
* Practice prevention strategies: Each bias page includes practical tips for overcoming that
  particular mental trap.
* Regular practice: Return regularly to reinforce your learning—understanding cognitive biases is an
  ongoing process!

## Frequently Asked Questions

## Common Questions About Cognitive Biases

### What are cognitive biases and why do they matter?

Cognitive biases are mental shortcuts or patterns in our thinking that can lead to errors in
judgment and decision-making. They matter because they impact nearly every aspect of our lives—from
personal choices to business decisions, social interactions, and even health outcomes. Common
examples include [confirmation bias][14], [anchoring bias][15], and [availability heuristic][16]. By
understanding these biases, you can make more rational choices, avoid common mental traps, and
ultimately improve your decision-making process.

### How can I use this site to improve my decision-making?

Great question! Our site offers several practical ways to boost your decision-making skills:
* Learn about specific biases: Browse our [comprehensive library][17] to understand how each bias
  affects your thinking.
* Try interactive exercises: Experience biases firsthand through our [quiz][18] and various
  simulations.
* Practice prevention strategies: Each bias page includes practical tips for overcoming that
  particular mental trap.
* Regular practice: Return regularly to reinforce your learning—understanding cognitive biases is an
  ongoing process!

[Take the Quiz][19][Play Matching Game][20][Try a Bias Test][21]

### Are some people more susceptible to cognitive biases than others?

Everyone experiences cognitive biases—they're part of being human! While no one is immune, research
suggests that factors like stress, time pressure, and cognitive load can make us more vulnerable to
these thinking errors. For instance, [Dunning-Kruger effect][22] shows how experts and novices
assess their abilities differently. The good news? Awareness is the first step toward improvement.
By learning to recognize these biases, anyone can work to mitigate their effects, regardless of
their natural tendencies. Education, critical thinking skills, and mindfulness practices have all
been shown to help reduce the impact of cognitive biases.

### How long does it take to overcome cognitive biases?

Overcoming cognitive biases isn't a one-time achievement but rather an ongoing process. While you
can start recognizing your own biases within days of learning about them, developing consistent
habits to counter these biases might take months or even become a lifelong practice. Biases like
[status quo bias][23] and [sunk cost fallacy][24] are particularly persistent because they're deeply
rooted in our psychology. Remember, the goal isn't to eliminate biases completely (that's
practically impossible!) but to recognize when they're influencing you and apply techniques to
minimize their impact. Even professional psychologists and behavioral economists continue to work on
their own biases—it's part of the human journey! We recommend regularly taking our [cognitive bias
quiz][25] to gauge your progress.

### Can cognitive biases ever be helpful?

Yes! Cognitive biases evolved for a reason. In many cases, these mental shortcuts help us make quick
decisions when time or information is limited. For example, the [availability heuristic][26] helps

# Homepage

DABATEM *(**Istanbul Center for Behavioral Sciences*** – formerly the *Istanbul Center for Behavior
Research and Therapy*) is an independent research center internationally recognized for its
pioneering research into mental health effects of wars, torture, and earthquakes, and their
effective treatment. It has been founded and is currently directed by [Professor Metin Başoğlu][56].

Mass trauma events affect large numbers of people and lead to a serious mental health problem around
the world. Effective dealing with this problem requires a mental healthcare model based on
interventions that are (1) theoretically sound, (2) proven to be effective, (3) brief, (4) easy to
train therapists in their delivery, (5) practicable in different cultures, and (6) suitable for
dissemination through media other than professional therapists, such as lay people, self-help tools,
and mass media. Current trauma treatments do not meet more than two or three of these requirements.

DABATEM has conducted extensive research over 40 years with trauma survivors to develop a
psychological treatment ([Control-Focused Behavioral Treatment – CFBT][57]), which meets all of the
above requirements. CFBT is a brief intervention that reduces traumatic stress by enhancing** sense
of control** over (or resilience against) trauma.  [Available evidence][58] suggests that it
achieves greater improvement than other evidence-based treatments.

DABATEM has also developed a [mental healthcare model][59] for earthquake survivors that
incorporates various brief and innovative applications of CFBT and treatment delivery strategies
that enable cost-effective dissemination of care to large survivor populations. Work is in progress
to develop a similar model for survivors of war and torture. A recent [treatment study][60] has
shown that CFBT is highly effective in survivors of war and torture.

# [More Thoughts on Suicide Prediction and Suicide Screening (from Craig Bryan, Ph.D.)][27]

[July 1, 2026][28] [johnsommersflanagan][29] [6 Comments][30]

Hi All,

Below, I’ve a pasted LinkedIn post from Dr. Craig Bryan, author of “Rethinking Suicide” and a
leading suicide researcher. At the bottom of his comments there’s a link to the article of which he
speaks.

Enjoy!

*****************

From Craig Bryan, LinkedIn – 6/29/2026

We keep trying to predict who will attempt suicide. A 15-year study suggests we’re asking the wrong
question.

Researchers followed 2,060 Brazilian children from age 10 into their mid-twenties—one of the longest
prospective suicide studies ever conducted outside a high-income country. They measured genetics,
perinatal history, family psychiatric illness, childhood adversity, cognition, and clinical
symptoms, then tested all of it together against who later attempted suicide.

The result: even with multiple domains of risk factors combined, prediction accuracy stayed modest
(AUC 0.665), barely above the ceiling seen across 50 years of suicide research. More sophisticated
machine learning models didn’t do any better than simple logistic regression.

Three factors stood out as consistent, actionable, and population-relevant: childhood threat
exposure (especially bullying), caregiver history of suicide attempts, and childhood externalizing
disorders. Bullying alone accounted for the largest share of preventable risk in the entire study.

The authors’ conclusion is blunt: distal childhood risk factors will likely never predict individual
suicide attempts with precision, because suicide is driven by acute, fast-moving processes that a
baseline assessment can’t capture. Trying to screen our way to safety has a ceiling. We hit it
decades ago.

The better investment may not be sharper prediction. It may be quieter, structural prevention like
anti-bullying programs, supporting parents with histories of suicidal behavior, and early
identification of behavioral disorders, the kind of intervention that helps a population, whether or
not we ever know which child needed it most.

**************************

Here’s the article link: [**https://lnkd.in/eRWtBiXK**][31]

I’m excited about Dr. Bryan’s post not because of the difficulties with prediction (which we’ve long
know), but because of the idea of moving upstream toward structural prevention. I also feel this
fits really well with what we’re trying to do with CAPE.

**Obviously, I love this quotation: **“Trying to screen our way to safety has a ceiling. We hit it
decades ago.”

Have a great evening!

JSF

club mentality that interfered with women’s salaries and promotions.

Let’s all agree on the following: All discrimination is wrong, allegations should be taken
seriously, and allegations deserve investigation.

But allegations are not facts.

Sadly, numerous Facebook posts, including an Op-Ed piece published in a Montana newspaper, repeat
allegations from 2021 to 2024 (when the case was settled). Beyond these allegations, they don’t

misogynistic.

# Laws of UX

Laws of UX is a collection of best practices that designers can consider when building user
interfaces.

The updated Laws of UX large format index poster is now available! Additions include Paradox of the
Active User, Selective Attention, Cognitive Bias, and more. [Check it out →][19]
* ## [Aesthetic-Usability Effect][20]
  
  Users often perceive aesthetically pleasing design as design that’s more usable.
* ## [Choice Overload][21]
  
  The tendency for people to get overwhelmed when they are presented with a large number of options,
  often used interchangeably with the term paradox of choice.
* ## [Chunking][22]
  
  A process by which individual pieces of an information set are broken down and then grouped
  together in a meaningful whole.
* ## [Cognitive Bias][23]
  
  A systematic error of thinking or rationality in judgment that influence our perception of the
  world and our decision-making ability.
* ## [Cognitive Load][24]
  
  The amount of mental resources needed to understand and interact with an interface.
* ## [Doherty Threshold][25]
  
  Productivity soars when a computer and its users interact at a pace (<400ms) that ensures that
  neither has to wait on the other.
* ## [Fitts’s Law][26]
  
  The time to acquire a target is a function of the distance to and size of the target.
* ## [Flow][27]
  
  The mental state in which a person performing some activity is fully immersed in a feeling of
  energized focus, full involvement, and enjoyment in the process of the activity.
* ## [Goal-Gradient Effect][28]
  
  The tendency to approach a goal increases with proximity to the goal.
* ## [Hick’s Law][29]
  
  The time it takes to make a decision increases with the number and complexity of choices.
* ## [Jakob’s Law][30]
  
  Users spend most of their time on other sites. This means that users prefer your site to work the
  same way as all the other sites they already know.
* ## [Law of Common Region][31]
  
  Elements tend to be perceived into groups if they are sharing an area with a clearly defined
  boundary.
* ## [Law of Proximity][32]
  
  Objects that are near, or proximate to each other, tend to be grouped together.
* ## [Law of Prägnanz][33]
  
  People will perceive and interpret ambiguous or complex images as the simplest form possible,
  because it is the interpretation that requires the least cognitive effort of us.
* ## [Law of Similarity][34]
  
  The human eye tends to perceive similar elements as a complete picture, shape, or group, even if
  those elements are separated.
* ## [Law of Uniform Connectedness][35]
  
  Elements that are visually connected are perceived as more related than elements with no
  connection.
* ## [Mental Model][36]
  
  A compressed model based on what we think we know about a system and how it works.
* ## [Miller’s Law][37]
  
  The average person can only keep 7 (plus or minus 2) items in their working memory.
* ## [Occam’s Razor][38]
  
  Among competing hypotheses that predict equally well, the one with the fewest assumptions should
  be selected.
* ## [Paradox of the Active User][39]
  
  Users never read manuals but start using the software immediately.
* ## [Pareto Principle][40]
  
  The Pareto principle states that, for many events, roughly 80% of the effects come from 20% of the
  causes.
* ## [Parkinson’s Law][41]
  
  Any task will inflate until all of the available time is spent.
* ## [Peak-End Rule][42]
  
  People judge an experience largely based on how they felt at its peak and at its end, rather than
  the total sum or average of every moment of the experience.
* ## [Postel’s Law][43]
  
  Be liberal in what you accept, and conservative in what you send.
* ## [Selective Attention][44]
  
  The process of focusing our attention only to a subset of stimuli in an environment — usually
  those related to our goals.
* ## [Serial Position Effect][45]
  
  Users have a propensity to best remember the first and last items in a series.
* ## [Tesler’s Law][46]
  
  Tesler's Law, also known as The Law of Conservation of Complexity, states that for any system
  there is a certain amount of complexity which cannot be reduced.
* ## [Von Restorff Effect][47]
  
  The Von Restorff effect, also known as The Isolation Effect, predicts that when multiple similar
  objects are present, the one that differs from the rest is most likely to be remembered.
* ## [Working Memory][48]
  
  A cognitive system that temporarily holds and manipulates information needed to complete tasks.
* ## [Zeigarnik Effect][49]
  
  People remember uncompleted or interrupted tasks better than completed tasks.

  A cognitive system that temporarily holds and manipulates information needed to complete tasks.
* ## [Zeigarnik Effect][49]
  
  People remember uncompleted or interrupted tasks better than completed tasks.

## 
## Richard J. McNally
## *Professor and Director of Clinical Training *

Dr. McNally studies anxiety disorders (e.g., social anxiety disorder), obsessive-compulsive disorder
(OCD), posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD), complicated grief, and depression. A major emphasis is
elucidating cognitive biases constitutive of these syndromes, and testing methods for reducing these
biases, thereby fostering symptom reduction. Hence, much of our work falls under the rubric of
experimental psychopathology as it aims to illuminate the mechanisms driving the etiology and
maintenance of emotional disorders. By clicking on the Research link above, you can read about
recent and ongoing projects in our lab.

RESILIENCE & HOPE

# Courage to heal. Strength to continue.

Misneach Mental Health is a therapy practice grounded in the belief that healing begins with
courage—the courage to show up, to face what hurts, and to keep moving forward even when the path
feels uncertain. The word Misneach (pronounced MISH-nukh) comes from Irish Gaelic and represents
courage, bravery, spirit, fortitude, hopefulness, and confidence. It reflects the inner strength
that allows people to rise again after being knocked down and to meet life’s challenges with
resilience and integrity. At Misneach Mental Health, the practice honors the bravery it takes to
seek support and the quiet strength found in choosing growth, healing, and self-understanding.

[Begin Your Healing
][3]
The Approach

## The Meaning of Misneach

Misneach (mish-nyokh) is a Gaelic word representing courage, spirit, and mental fortitude. It is
more than just bravery; it is the inner strength required to face adversity with hope and the
resilience to continue even when the path is difficult. At Misneach Mental Health, our philosophy is
rooted in this concept—honoring each individual's innate capacity for healing and growth. We believe
that therapy is a collaborative journey where professional expertise meets the client's personal
courage, creating a space where transformation and lasting well-being become possible.

## About Kim

Kim is trained in Adaptive Internal Relational Network Therapy (AIR) and Eye Movement
Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR). She has worked extensively with children, adolescents, and
families in school settings, and has also served the State of Minnesota through roles with both the
Department of Corrections and the Department of Health Services. Kim’s clinical work is grounded in
a strengths-based perspective, incorporating motivational interviewing and solution-focused
interventions, with a strong foundation in Adlerian therapy. She is deeply committed to helping
clients develop their capacity to heal from trauma and move toward becoming their most authentic,
empowered selves. Kim holds a Master’s degree in Adlerian Psychology with a focus on Co-Occurring
Disorders from Adler Graduate School, a Master’s degree in Forensic Psychology from Argosy
University, and a Bachelor of Arts in Criminal Justice from St. Cloud State University. She received
her EMDR training through an EMDRIA-approved provider. Kim is honored to support the men and women
who serve their communities and country, including military personnel, veterans, first responders,
firefighters, and law enforcement officers. She recognizes the distinct challenges inherent in these
professions and is committed to providing a safe, respectful, and confidential space for healing and
restoration. Misneach Mental Health is dedicated to evidence-based, trauma-informed care tailored to
the needs of active-duty service members, veterans, and public safety professionals. The practice
understands the occupational stress, cumulative trauma, and high-risk demands that can impact mental
health. Clients can expect a supportive, confidential environment focused on resilience, effective
coping, and long-term psychological well-being.

## Types of Therapeutic Interventions

##### Cognitive-Behavioral Therapies

Focus on identifying and changing unhelpful thought patterns and behaviors.

##### Cognitive Restructuring

Challenging irrational beliefs.

##### Behavioral Activation

Increasing engagement in positive activities.

##### Mindfulness

Focusing on the present moment.

##### Psychodynamic Therapy

Explores past experiences and relationships to understand current patterns.

##### Humanistic Therapy

Emphasizes self-exploration, personal growth, and unconditional positive regard.

##### Interpersonal Therapy (IPT)

Focuses on improving relationships and social functioning, often for depression.

##### Communication & Skills Training

Focuses on building interpersonal skills, conflict resolution, and problem-solving for individuals
or families.

##### EMDR (Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing)

Helps reprocess traumatic memories.

##### Psychoeducation

Teaching clients about their conditions and coping skills.

##### Motivational Interviewing (MI)

Helps clients find internal motivation for change.

##### Supportive Therapy

Provides empathy, validation, and active listening.

##### Adlerian

Goal-oriented, strengths-based intervention that helps individuals understand lifestyle, sense of
belonging, and purposeful behavior to foster social interest and positive change.

##### DBT skills

A structured, evidence-based intervention that teaches mindfulness, distress tolerance, emotion
regulation, and interpersonal effectiveness to help individuals manage intense emotions.

# NHS website for England Find information and services to help you manage your health

## [Health A to Z][8]

Find out about conditions, symptoms, medicines, tests and treatments, including when to get help

## [NHS services][9]

Find out about NHS services including GPs, pharmacies, prescriptions, hospitals and dentists

## Manage your health

* [ View your test results ][11]
* [ Appointments and bookings at your GP surgery ][12]

* [ Find a GP ][17]
* [ Find NHS talking therapies for anxiety and depression ][18]

[ Find other NHS services ][19]

### Help from NHS 111

If you're worried about a symptom and not sure what help you need, NHS 111 can tell you what to do
next.

Go to [111.nhs.uk][20] or [call 111][21].

For a life-threatening emergency call 999.

## Featured
* ### [ Book a COVID-19 vaccination appointment ][22]
  
  If you're eligible for the spring COVID-19 vaccine, you can book a vaccination appointment now
* ### [ Get healthcare cover abroad with a UK GHIC or EHIC ][23]
  
  Get or renew your health insurance card to help you get healthcare in the EU and some other
  countries
* ### [ Refer yourself for help for back and joint problems ][24]
  
  Get NHS help from community musculoskeletal (MSK) services, like physiotherapy, for back and joint
  problems

## More information and advice
* ## [Vaccinations][25]
  
  Information about vaccinations for babies, children and adults, including why they're important
  and how to get them
* ## [COVID-19][26]
  
  Advice about COVID-19, including symptoms, treatments and how to avoid catching and spreading it.
* ## [Baby][27]
  
  A guide to everything you need to know about caring for a baby
* ## [Women's health][28]
  
  Information and support on health, wellbeing, conditions and screening
* ## [Contraception][29]
  
  Information about different types of contraception, including where to get them and how well they
  work

# Feel better with interactive mental health tools

Simple practices you can use right now. Calm the body, steady emotions, and focus on small steps.
Tools are evidence based, private by design, and fast on phones.

[Open Toolkit][16] [Get Support][17]

**Important:** if you are in immediate danger, contact local emergency services.

[TIPP][18] [5 4 3 2 1][19] [Breathing][20] [Safe Place][21] [Relax][22] [Urge][23] [Facts][24]
[Opposite][25]

## Choose a simple path

[
🧭

### Self Discovery Tests

Quick check ins to learn about mood, stress, and habits.

][26] [
🎯

### Wellness Games and Exercises

Practice skills for focus, calm, and motivation.

][27] [
🤝

Find a professional for private, personal help.

][28]

## Popular right now
* [
  
  ### Breathing Anchor
  
  Steady breath, settle nerves, and regain focus.
  
  ][29]
* [
  
  ### Focus Timer
  
  Work in short sprints with gentle breaks.
  
  ][30]
* [
  
  ### Thought Reframe Studio
  
  Spot thinking traps and try a kinder view.
  
  ][31]
* [
  
  ### Gratitude Galaxy
  
  Log small wins and watch your stars grow.
  
  ][32]
* [
  
  ### Opposite Action Planner
  
  Choose the next helpful action when urges pull you off track.
  
  ][33]
* [
  
  ### Digital Zen Garden
  
  Play and settle attention with a calm space.
  
  ][34]
* [
  
  ### Sensory Grounding
  
  Use the five senses to return to the present.
  
  ][35]
* [
  
  ### TIPP Crisis Kit
  
  Lower arousal fast with safe, short actions.
  
  ][36]

## How interactive mental health tools help

The site focuses on small skills you can practice in minutes. You can calm the body, label thoughts,
and plan the next step. The tools draw from CBT, DBT, mindfulness, and behavior change. Pages are
private by design and mobile first.

## Frequently asked questions

Do these tools replace therapy

No. These are self help practices. They do not diagnose or replace care. Use Get Support if you want
to work with a professional.

How is my data handled

If a tool saves entries, it uses your browser. Nothing goes to a server. You can clear data by
clearing site storage.

What if I feel worse

Pause and try a calming tool like Breathing Anchor or 5 4 3 2 1 Grounding. If distress continues,
contact local emergency services.

How often should I practice

Short and steady works best. Try 2 to 10 minutes once or twice a day. Repeat what helps.

Where should I start

Pick one tool that fits now. For high arousal try TIPP. For thinking traps try Thought Reframe
Studio.

## Trust and science

Learn more from [NIMH][37], [APA][38], [WHO][39].

## Important safety information

These tools are educational self help. They are not therapy or a diagnosis. If you face an
emergency, contact local emergency services. For non emergency help, visit Get Support.

Exercises][42] · [Get Support][43]

Why this matters

## Healthcare's integration debt is compounding.

Every healthcare team carries the same technical scar tissue: a custom HL7 parser nobody wants to
touch, a FHIR layer that mostly works, and integration timelines that double whenever a system
changes.

01

### Integration takes quarters when every site is custom.

Undocumented Z-segments, brittle transforms, and local EHR quirks force teams to rebuild the same
interfaces over and over.

02

### Compliance lands on top of already fragile pipelines.

HIPAA, GDPR, ENS, and EHDS are not optional features. If governance is bolted on later, every new

# Психологическая помощь с тревогой и страхами в Москве и онлайн

Если вы сталкиваетесь с:

## Паническими атаками

[image(1)]

У вас непредсказуемые приступы сильного страха, сопровождаемые такими симптомами: сердцебиение,
ощущение удушья, тремор, потливость, головокружение, слабость, тошнота, дереализация и
деперсонализация. Приступы сопровождаются страхом смерти, потери контроля или сумасшествия.

## Страхом общения

[0a361b1821a63e43dbb2f5904b136ab15]

Вы боитесь оценки со стороны других людей. Вас пугает, что в процессе общения у вас будут трястись
руки, дрожать голос, вы покраснеете, вспотеете, скажете глупость или будете казаться неловким.
Бывает, что вы откладываете важные звонки, избегаете выступлений или поездок в метро.

## Тревогой и беспокойством

[Glavnaya21]

Вы постоянно в тревоге по самым разным причинам. То вы беспокоитесь о работе, то про здоровье, то о
благополучии близких, то не можете уснуть перед поездкой в отпуск. Вы устали от бесконечного
«мысленного диалога», при котором ваш внутренний голос постоянно рисует катастрофические сценарии.

Вы пытались справиться самостоятельно, читали умные книги, уговаривали себя успокоиться, но не
смотря на усилия, паника, страх и тревога возвращаются снова. Обратитесь за психологической помощью.

## Чем может помочь психолог?

[icon]Вы можете справиться с приступами иррационального страха, тревогой и паническими атаками

[icon]Вы улучшите качество своей жизни

## Меня зовут Васильева Ольга Борисовна

[[vasileva]][15]

### [Васильева Ольга Борисовна][16]

Я частнопрактикующий когнитивно-поведенческий психолог.

Я не даю волшебных таблеток и не обещаю исцеления за одну сессию. Шаг за шагом я помогаю вам
разобраться в причинах проблем и дать инструменты, которые сначала помогут справиться с симптомами,
а затем будут помогать вам в будущем.

У меня большой опыт работы как с клиентами с тревогой и страхами, так и с теми, кому психиатр
поставил диагноз тревожное расстройство:
* Паническим расстройством
* Генерализованным тревожным расстройством
* Социальной тревожностью
* Изолированными фобиями

А также с клиентами, имеющими диагнозы ОКР, БАР, депрессия.

Запишитесь на консультацию очно рядом с метро Римская или он-лайн.

[icon]Снижение общего уровня тревожности. Вы сможете снизить уровень своего беспокойства.

**[icon]**Свобода передвижения. Вы сможете ездить в метро, электричках или ходить в торговые центры.

## Почему стоит обратиться ко мне
* **Прозрачность работы.** Я объясняю логику каждого упражнения. Никакой магии, шаманства и
  эзотерики. Только понятная биология и психология поведения.
* **Ориентация на краткосрочную работу.** Моя задача — сделать вас самостоятельными. Мы не будем
  ходить годами. Средняя продолжительность работы над тревожным запросом — от 8 до 15 встреч. Первые
  устойчивые улучшения вы заметите уже через 2–3 сессии, и это подкреплено исключительно вашими
  действиями между встречами.
* **Доказательный подход.** Я использую протоколы, рекомендованные мировым психологическим

# Психологическая помощь с тревогой и страхами в Москве и онлайн

Если вы сталкиваетесь с:

## Паническими атаками

[image(1)]

У вас непредсказуемые приступы сильного страха, сопровождаемые такими симптомами: сердцебиение,
ощущение удушья, тремор, потливость, головокружение, слабость, тошнота, дереализация и
деперсонализация. Приступы сопровождаются страхом смерти, потери контроля или сумасшествия.

## Страхом общения

[0a361b1821a63e43dbb2f5904b136ab15]

Вы боитесь оценки со стороны других людей. Вас пугает, что в процессе общения у вас будут трястись
руки, дрожать голос, вы покраснеете, вспотеете, скажете глупость или будете казаться неловким.
Бывает, что вы откладываете важные звонки, избегаете выступлений или поездок в метро.

## Тревогой и беспокойством

[Glavnaya21]

Вы постоянно в тревоге по самым разным причинам. То вы беспокоитесь о работе, то про здоровье, то о
благополучии близких, то не можете уснуть перед поездкой в отпуск. Вы устали от бесконечного
«мысленного диалога», при котором ваш внутренний голос постоянно рисует катастрофические сценарии.

Вы пытались справиться самостоятельно, читали умные книги, уговаривали себя успокоиться, но не
смотря на усилия, паника, страх и тревога возвращаются снова. Обратитесь за психологической помощью.

## Чем может помочь психолог?

[icon]Вы можете справиться с приступами иррационального страха, тревогой и паническими атаками

[icon]Вы улучшите качество своей жизни

[icon]Вы получите свободу для того, чтобы путешествовать, строить карьеру и личные отношения

## Меня зовут Васильева Ольга Борисовна

[[vasileva]][15]

### [Васильева Ольга Борисовна][16]

Я частнопрактикующий когнитивно-поведенческий психолог.

Я не даю волшебных таблеток и не обещаю исцеления за одну сессию. Шаг за шагом я помогаю вам
разобраться в причинах проблем и дать инструменты, которые сначала помогут справиться с симптомами,
а затем будут помогать вам в будущем.

У меня большой опыт работы как с клиентами с тревогой и страхами, так и с теми, кому психиатр
поставил диагноз тревожное расстройство:
* Паническим расстройством
* Генерализованным тревожным расстройством
* Социальной тревожностью
* Изолированными фобиями

А также с клиентами, имеющими диагнозы ОКР, БАР, депрессия.

Запишитесь на консультацию очно рядом с метро Римская или он-лайн.

Перестать тревожиться

## Результаты, которые вы увидите после курса консультирования

[icon]Снижение общего уровня тревожности. Вы сможете снизить уровень своего беспокойства.

**[icon]**Свобода передвижения. Вы сможете ездить в метро, электричках или ходить в торговые центры.

**[icon]**Избавление от желания всем понравится и всем угодить. Вы сможете говорить «нет» без
чувства вины.

## Почему стоит обратиться ко мне
* **Прозрачность работы.** Я объясняю логику каждого упражнения. Никакой магии, шаманства и
  эзотерики. Только понятная биология и психология поведения.
* **Ориентация на краткосрочную работу.** Моя задача — сделать вас самостоятельными. Мы не будем
  ходить годами. Средняя продолжительность работы над тревожным запросом — от 8 до 15 встреч. Первые
  устойчивые улучшения вы заметите уже через 2–3 сессии, и это подкреплено исключительно вашими
  действиями между встречами.
* **Доказательный подход.** Я использую протоколы, рекомендованные мировым психологическим
  сообществом для работы именно с тревожными расстройствами.

## Нужен ли врач-психиатр?

[obsled]К психиатрам имеет смысл обращаться, если вы хотите узнать точный диагноз и получить рецепты
на лекарства. Если вы стоите перед выбором врача, то лучше обратиться к доказательному психиатру.

Вы можете прийти ко мне после встречи с психиатром. Тогда подготовьте для меня код или название
диагноза, который он поставил, а также список и дозировки препаратов, которые вы принимаете.

Если вы пришли сначала ко мне и я посчитаю, что вам следует посетить соматического врача или
